items.markdown:
Yes. For a blue Staffordshire Bull Terrier (“Staffy”), I’d start with **The Kennel Club’s Find a Puppy** service rather than buying from a generic puppy-advertising site. You can filter for Staffordshire Bull Terriers, health-tested parents and breed-standard colours. Blue is an accepted Staffordshire Bull Terrier colour in the UK breed standard. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/find-an-assured-breeder/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?gad=1&utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

### Where to look

- [thekennelclub.org.uk](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/find-a-puppy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) — use the Staffordshire Bull Terrier breed filter and select health-tested parents/breed-standard colours.
- **The Staffordshire Bull Terrier Club** The Staffordshire Bull Terrier Club — a useful route to breed-specific contacts and advice.
- If you're willing to travel around the North West, there are several breeders listed locally, including [Ravenscroft Staffordshire Bull Terries Puppies](https://ukstaffypups.uk/) in Liverpool and [Earlsgrave Bull Terriers](https://www.earlsgravebullterriers.com/) in Kidderminster. **I wouldn't treat a business listing or reviews as evidence that a breeder is responsible**, though; verify their health testing and breeding practices yourself.

### What I'd ask the breeder

The big thing is **don't let “blue” become more important than health and temperament**. The Kennel Club specifically recommends Staffordshire Bull Terrier breeders screen for hereditary cataracts (HC-HSF4-2), L-2-HGA, elbow dysplasia and eye problems, with genetic diversity also being a consideration. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?gad=1&utm_source=chatgpt.com) [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/media/qvffqvwg/kc_health_standard.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

Ask:

1. **“Can I see the mother's health-test certificates and the father's?”**

 - HC-HSF4-2 (hereditary cataracts)
- L-2-HGA
- BVA/KC elbow testing
- BVA/KC/ISDS eye testing, including litter screening where applicable. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?gad=1&utm_source=chatgpt.com)
2. **“What are the KC registration numbers of both parents?”**
 You can then independently check their recorded health results rather than relying solely on screenshots or verbal assurances.
3. **“Can I meet the puppy with its mother, at the place where it was raised?”**
 This is particularly important. The Kennel Club advises buyers to meet the breeder and see both the dam and puppy before committing to purchase. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/find-an-assured-breeder/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
4. **“How has the litter been socialised?”**
 Ask about children, visitors, household noises, handling, other dogs, car journeys, grooming and being left alone.
5. **“Have there been any health or temperament problems in previous litters or relatives?”**
 A good breeder shouldn't be defensive about discussing problems.
6. **“Why did you choose these two dogs to breed?”**
 You want an answer centred on health, temperament and maintaining the breed—not simply “because blue puppies sell.”
7. **“How many litters has the mother had, and how old is she?”**
8. **“What exactly comes with the puppy?”**
 Ask about microchipping, vaccination, worming, insurance, registration/pedigree documentation, food and the puppy's medical records. The Kennel Club recommends providing vaccination/worming information and copies of the parents' health certificates. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/dog-breeding/first-time-breeders/selling-your-puppies/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### Red flags 🚩

I'd walk away if the breeder:

- Won't let you see the puppy **with its mother**.
- Wants to meet in a car park or deliver the puppy without you visiting.
- Has lots of different breeds or constantly has puppies available.
- Says **“blue is rare, so they're £X more”** without being interested in health and temperament.
- Can't produce verifiable health-test results.
- Wants a deposit before you've properly seen the litter.
- Is reluctant to answer questions about previous litters or health problems.
- Advertises unusual colours as “rare/exotic” and makes colour the main selling point.

Also, don't assume that **KC registered = health tested**. Registration and health screening are separate things; check the actual test results. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/find-an-assured-breeder/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/dog-breeding/first-time-breeders/health-screening-a-step-by-step-guide/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

If you tell me **your approximate budget and how far you're willing to travel from Manchester**, I can search current UK listings and help you make a shortlist of blue Staffy litters, then check what health information each breeder provides.
